aoi_name: Sweihan dune field, NW of Al Ain

baseline.note: velocities from the Landsat 8/9 OLI network (12 November scenes, 66 pairs); the Landsat 7 scenes (2000-11-27, 2001-11-30) are used only as a long-baseline check

speed_note: speeds are of the 1762 dune windows (480 m) with detected motion (86.2 % of 2045 valid); the other 283 move slower than their detection limit (median 0.36 m/yr) and are not in these statistics. Max detected 3.87 m/yr. uncertainty_myr = median calibrated 1-sigma per component.
wind_agreement_note: mean |heading - RDD| over detected windows, RDD 87.2 deg (MERRA-2 2000-2024). The regime is bimodal (RDP/DP 0.432), but here the dunes follow the resultant: the field-median heading 82.9 deg is 4.3 deg from RDD, 29.6 deg from the strongest (north-westerly) mode and 82.9 deg from the opposing one; per-window median difference 10.9 deg.

published.reference: No published dune-migration rate for Sweihan (Phase 1b literature search, docs/research/aoi-sweihan-liwa.md section 5)
published.our_value: 1.15 m/yr median (10-90 %: 0.55-1.82) toward 83 deg, 2013-2025, windows with detected motion
published.note: No comparison is possible. The nearest local number, the Seih Al Hama thesis value '3.32 m', has no stated time base and is from a different field 45 km away, so it is not used. The Landsat 7 epochs (2000, 2001) give the same speed over 2000-2025 as 2013-2025, which is the only long-term check available.

second_dataset.their_value: HLS S30 (Sentinel-2, independent): field median 0.562 m/yr toward 85.9 deg; per-window correlation with Landsat r = 0.433 (E), 0.368 (N); its detection limit 0.913 m/yr, motion detected in 30.6 % of windows. HLS L30 (same Landsat instruments, not independent): 0.942 m/yr toward 79.2 deg, r = 0.736/0.553
second_dataset.our_value: Landsat pan 15 m over the same years: field median 1.013 m/yr toward 80.2 deg (S30 years); 1.079 m/yr toward 83.6 deg (L30 years)
second_dataset.note: The independent Sentinel-2 check agrees on direction (field headings 5.7 deg apart) but gives about half the speed (0.562 vs 1.013 m/yr) and agrees only weakly window by window (r 0.433/0.368); at 30 m its detection limit (0.913 m/yr) is close to most measured speeds. Where Landsat speeds exceed twice the detection limit (1348 windows) headings differ by a median 14.7 deg. HLS L30 agrees better (heading within 4.5 deg, speed 0.942 vs 1.079 m/yr, r 0.736/0.553) but uses the same Landsat instruments, so it only shows the result survives a different band, resolution and processing.

data_handling.display_only_frames: 4 Landsat 7 frames acquired after the 31 May 2003 scan-line-corrector failure (2005-11-09, 2008-11-17, 2011-11-10, 2012-11-12) are shown on the timeline as images only, stripes left as no-data; they are not used in any number in this file (see frames/manifest.json observed_display_only).
data_handling.notes: 8 November candidate scenes rejected in notebook 01 (cloud/shadow/haze/coverage; listed in pipeline/outputs/sweihan/scene_rejections.csv); Landsat 7 used only before the 31 May 2003 SLC failure. Clouds/shadows: Landsat QA_PIXEL bits 0-4 (dilated 1 px), HLS Fmask bits 1-3. Of 10100 tracking windows, 3081 lie outside the box and 4921 are mostly non-dune (vegetation, WorldCover, OSM, hand-drawn change areas); of the 2098 dune windows 2.53 % had too few valid pairs. Window-pair observations rejected: 5.76 % (weak match below the false-match threshold, displacement beyond the reliable range, network outliers).

limits: Detected dune windows move a median 1.15 m/yr (10-90 %: 0.55-1.82, max 3.87), i.e. roughly 15-45 m in 25 years; 14 % of valid dune windows move below the detection limit (median 0.36 m/yr) and have no measured direction.

Reach years forecast the migration of dune forms (slip-face advance), not wind-blown sand crossing a road, which happens wherever a road borders loose sand, whatever the dunes do (see borders_free_sand in targets.geojson).
At about 1 m/yr one 15 m pixel is about 15 years of motion, so reach years for targets near the sand carry an edge uncertainty of +-7.5 m plus the outline uncertainty of the target.
Most targets are not reached by 2050; targets flagged 'sand at edge now' already have migrating sand within that edge uncertainty.
The projection is advection along the measured 2013-2025 motion, assuming those conditions continue; it does not model dune deformation, merging, splitting or growth.
Vegetation, windbreaks, sand fences, levelling, construction and climate change alter the outcome.

Motion is measured in 480 m windows: it is the motion of the small dunes (spacing ~73-99 m) and sand sheets inside, not of the large ridges they ride on; the motion of those ridge bodies is not measured (the body-scale matcher failed its known-shift test).
Only 12 large dunes (13-45 m high) are outlined, from NASADEM (February 2000) shifted to 2025; the small dunes that carry most of the motion are represented by the velocity grid, not by polygons.
The independent Sentinel-2 (HLS S30) check agrees on direction but gives about half the speed; HLS L30 agrees better but uses the same Landsat instruments.
No published migration rate exists for Sweihan, so there is nothing to compare against.
MERRA-2 wind is a ~0.5 x 0.625 deg reanalysis of hourly means; absolute drift potential is approximate and the regime is bimodal.

Farm targets are vegetated plots (HLS NDVI, last year) plus OSM farmland, which here includes the abandoned south-east farm grid and graded strips; built-up targets include large OSM landuse=residential zones, so a 'built-up area' hit can mean sand reaching the edge of zoned, partly empty land rather than buildings.

Results are valid for this box and 2013-2025 only; about 63 % of the box is masked as non-dune or changed ground (hand-drawn masks with reasons in pipeline/site_config/sweihan/), and nothing outside the box is assessed.

threat.reach_definition: Migrating dune sand (free sand inside a window whose dune-form migration is detected), carried along its measured heading at its measured speed, arrives at the edge of the target footprint (road: OSM centre line +- class half width incl. shoulders; farm: HLS vegetated outline; built-up: OSM outline).
excludes: wind-blown sand crossing or settling on a target
motion below the detection limit (no direction: never a hit)
dune deformation, merging, growth, levelling or stabilisation
threat.speeds: median = measured window speed v; fast = v + sigma; slow = v - sigma (sigma = calibrated per-component 1-sigma; 84th/16th percentiles of the speed)
threat.years: hit_year_min = floor(t0 + gap_lo / fast); hit_year_max = ceil(t0 + gap_hi / slow); gap = distance from the source pixel centre to the footprint along the heading minus 7.5 m, +-(7.5 m + outline uncertainty: roads/buildings 5 m, farms 15 m); t0 = 2025-11-08; earliest over all sand reaching the target; null if the fast case does not arrive by 2100

confirmation.rule: speed agrees if a check's field-median speed is within 15% of Landsat's over the same windows and years; heading agrees if the field-median headings differ by <= 20 deg (Landsat 7: per-window east and north correlations both >= 0.8). confirmed = the independent Sentinel-2 check (HLS S30) agrees; partly_confirmed = only the partly independent Landsat 7 long baseline agrees; not_confirmed = neither. HLS L30 uses the same Landsat 8/9 instruments and is shown for context only.
